description:
Convert HTML and XML to PDF Using CSS

PDF Chemistry allows you to obtain PDF output from HTML or XML documents simply by styling them with CSS. It is a CSS Paged Media processor based on the open-source Apache FOP XSL-FO engine. Its main purpose is to provide you with a simple tool that allows you to leverage your CSS knowledge to create printable deliverables. It is particularly useful for generating technical documentation.
PDF Chemistry comes integrated with Oxygen XML Editor/Author but it is also available as a separate product for easy integration with automated processes. This means you can use an integration server to run the transformations to publish the PDF output or simply use a command-line interface to run the transformations. Note that the separate product requires its own license key.
Oxygen PDF Chemistry 29 produces cleaner, more professional layouts with smarter page breaks and positioning around floating elements and the option to keep spanned table cells on a single page. Multilingual publishing is easier with character-level font fallback for mixed-language content and language-specific SVG variants chosen automatically, and font rules can now be applied to MathML elements directly from CSS.
Core

Character-Level Fallback Fonts

For DITA to PDF publishing, you can use the new enable.character.level.font.fallback parameter to enable character-level font fallbacks so that mixed-language content (for example, Latin and non-Latin) is rendered correctly in the same document.
Apply Font Rules to MathML Elements

Font properties (such as font-family, font-size, and font-weight) can now be applied to MathML elements directly from CSS.
Smarter Page Break Handling Around Floating Elements

PDF output now handles page breaks more intelligently around floating elements, helping to prevent content from overflowing at the bottom of pages and producing cleaner, more professional layouts.
Read 4 more changes
Improved Positioning for Floating Elements in PDF Output

Floating elements are now positioned more accurately in PDF output to help prevent them from overlapping surrounding text.
Prevent Page Breaks Inside Table Cells

It is now possible to prevent page breaks inside spanned table cells in PDF output (for example, by using page-break-inside="avoid").
Prevent Page Breaks Only if Content Fits on the Page

You can avoid page breaks only if the content fits on a page by using the new -oxy-avoid-if-fits value in CSS properties that control page breaks in PDF output (for example, break-inside:-oxy-avoid-if-fits, break-before:-oxy-avoid-if-fits, break-after:-oxy-avoid-if-fits).
Use Language-Specific SVG Variants in PDF Output

PDF output now displays the appropriate language variant for SVG images that use the <switch> element, matching the xml:lang attribute where the image is located. This reduces the number of individual graphics needed and lowers the maintenance effort for image-intensive documentation.
